title: Peregrine Labs renewal — surge-handshake sizing checklist & evidence request
text:
Peregrine Labs renewal — surge-handshake sizing checklist & evidence request

['From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@peregrinelabs.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@peregrinelabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peregrine Labs renewal — surge-handshake sizing checklist & evidence request

Hi Elena / Rajiv,

We’re starting the renewal sizing conversation for your Dedicated fleet and want to make sure our recommendations map to what you actually saw over the last quarter. To prepare a clean options package, can you share the following (attachments are fine):

- p50 / p95 token/sec and request/sec for the last 90 days (daily granularity preferred)
- three largest concurrency peaks (time + duration) and the model mix during those peaks (e.g., gpt-*-like, M2-multimodal)
- average and 95th percentile sequence lengths for generation workloads
- retention/embedding reuse patterns (do you reuse KV caches or re-encode frequently?)
- any upcoming product changes that could drive >2x spikes (model launches, batch inference jobs)

I’ve attached a small export template (usage_export_q1.csv) to make sharing easier. If it’s easier, a link to your usage dashboard snapshot is fine too.

Tentative timeline: we’d like to present a two-option proposal (conservative reserved + elastic surge) by Aug 18 so Peregrine can pick a path during the week of renewal. Are you available for a 30-minute call next week to align?

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
', 'From: Elena Torres <elena@peregrinelabs.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@peregrinelabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine Labs renewal — surge-handshake sizing checklist & evidence request

Hi Kim — thanks for the template. Attaching a quick CSV (peregrine_q2_usage_summary.csv) that shows daily token counts, peak concurrency events, and model tags for Q2. High level:

- Typical p50 throughput: ~420 tokens/sec across requests (mostly text-gen)
- Observed p95 bursts: 2.6k - 3.4k tokens/sec tied to a small user cohort on the East region (peaks lasted 12-45m)
- Recent product change: we rolled a multimodal preview to a subset on Jun 20 that caused short spikes (images + long prompts)
- KV reuse: ~65% reuse for the conversational flows, but batch scoring re-encodes embeddings frequently

We can do a call — I’m available Aug 18 afternoon PT. Also attaching the CSV export. Let me know what you want us to prepare for the meeting.

Best,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure, Peregrine Labs
', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Peregrine Labs renewal — quick sizing thoughts from usage snapshot

Kim / Ben — I pulled the attached usage CSV and sketched an initial sizing calc (sizing_calc_v1.xlsx). Notes / assumptions:

- Baseline: current committed capacity is 4 x h100-equivalent slots; observed steady-state p50 matches that envelope but p95 bursts exceed by ~2.5x during peaks shown on Jun 20 and Jul 11.
- Model mix: ~85% text generation (short-medium sequences), ~15% multimodal/long-seq during spikes. Multimodal jobs increase GPU memory pressure and KV cache churn.

Two viable options we should show Peregrine:

1) Conservative reserved upgrade:
- Move to 6x H100-equivalent reserved slots (static pool)
- Benefit: low routing complexity, predictable latency; expected p50 generation latency ~55ms, p95 under 200ms during modeled peaks
- Draw: ~+48% monthly cost vs current commit

2) Elastic reserved + burst pool (recommended for revenue predictability):
- Keep 4x reserved, add a 2x hot-burst pool that can be invoked for up to 60 minutes per event with automated routing and capacity handshake
- Implement KV prefix caching for the conversational flows (push cache on warmup) to reduce demand during bursts (expected 20–30% peak reduction)
- Expected latency: p50 ~65ms, p95 ~220ms during bursts; cost delta ~+22% on committed fees plus metered burst usage

Operational asks if they pick option 2:
- Confirm region(s) to seed burst pool (us-west vs us-east)
- Provide 7×24 observability access for first 30 days so we can validate cache warmup behavior
- SOC2 audit/retention requirements to attach to the contract

I included a conservative sensitivity sheet in the workbook; numbers can be tuned on the call.

-rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@peregrinelabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed options for renewal — Peregrine Labs (summary & next steps)

Hi Elena / Rajiv,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the usage export — helpful context. Based on Rishi’s sizing (attached) we’ve put together two clear options so Peregrine can pick the one that best fits your reliability and cost posture. I’ve attached a one-page summary (peregrine_option_summary.pdf) that we’ll present on our call. High-level:

Option A — Reserved upgrade to 6x H100-eq
- Predictable throughput, lowest routing complexity
- Cost impact: ~+48% on committed monthly fee

Option B — Reserved 4x + 2x hot-burst pool (recommended)
- Keeps base commit lower, covers peaks with metered burst consumption and KV cache tricks to reduce headroom needed
- Cost impact: ~+22% committed + metered burst; projected 30% lower total expected spend vs Option A for the workloads you shared

Compliance / procurement notes:
- We can include SOC2 attestation and an audit-log export cadence in the contract (you asked about logs)
- We’ll need to know which region(s) you want the burst pool seeded in (us-west recommended given your East cohort is triggering spikes)
- If you want a tech walkthrough, Rishi will be on the call to go over routing/fallbacks and cache warmups

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-minute call to review and pick option — proposed windows Aug 19 10:00–11:00 PT or Aug 19 15:00–16:00 PT
2) If Option B chosen, we’ll deliver an implementation checklist and a 30-day validation window
3) If Option A chosen, we’ll prepare a reserved amendment and timeline for migration

Please let me know which time works and any additional items you want on the agenda.

Thanks — Kim
--
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
', 'From: Elena Torres <elena@peregrinelabs.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@peregrinelabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed options for renewal — Peregrine Labs (summary & next steps)

Kim — thank you, Option B looks like the best fit for us (we want to avoid committing to 6x unless traffic stabilizes). Aug 19 10:00 PT works for a call.

Pre-call checklist we’ll bring:
- Confirmed full-day usage export for last 90 days (we’ll send a raw dump)
- SOC2 report and the retention/audit log details (we need the exact ingestion format)
- Region confirmation: let’s seed burst pool in us-west, and add us-east as a fallback later

Can Rishi prepare a 10-minute slide on cache warmup strategy and how the burst handshake works end-to-end? If we’re good after the call, we’ll move to an amendment for the reserved+burst path with a 30-day validation clause.

See you tomorrow at 10.

Best,
Elena
', '(attachments referenced in thread: usage_export_q1.csv, peregrine_q2_usage_summary.csv, sizing_calc_v1.xlsx, peregrine_option_summary.pdf)']
